question: A nurse on the ward realises that a woman has been given the wrong dose of a drug. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Write the error in the register and tell the nurse on duty
option_2: Assess the woman, inform the doctor, and record the error at once
option_3: Give the woman an antidote before informing anyone
option_4: Wait to see whether the woman has any ill effect
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Assess the woman, inform the doctor, and record the error at once

Clinical Rationale: After a medication error the nurse FIRST assesses the woman, informs the doctor, and records the error, so that the harm is limited and the event is reported.

Key Clue: a woman given the wrong dose of a drug

Priority Principle: Medication error

Why Not Others: (a) Writing the record is done after the woman is assessed and seen; (c) An antidote is never given before the doctor is informed; (d) Waiting to watch her delays the care that she may need.

PGI Exam Trap: The nurse waits to see whether the woman has any ill effect.

5-Second Recall: Assess, inform the doctor, then record the error.

PNC Exam Pearl: Care first, report at once.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is to collect a midstream urine sample for culture. Which is the BEST order of the steps that the nurse should follow?
option_1: Ask him to pass urine into the bottle at any time of day
option_2: Collect the FIRST urine that comes out and send it for culture
option_3: Explain the step, clean the area, pass the FIRST urine, then collect the middle
option_4: Collect the urine after the bladder has been emptied fully
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Explain the step, clean the area, pass the FIRST urine, then collect the middle

Clinical Rationale: For a midstream sample the nurse explains the step, cleans the area, discards the FIRST urine and collects the middle part of the stream.

Key Clue: collecting a midstream urine sample from a man

Priority Principle: Midstream urine collection

Why Not Others: (a) The sample is collected in a clean, clean-catch manner and not at any time; (b) The first urine is flushed out because it carries the germs of the tube; (d) Urine from an empty bladder cannot be collected as a sample.

PGI Exam Trap: The FIRST urine is collected for the culture.

5-Second Recall: Clean, then collect the middle of the stream.

PNC Exam Pearl: The middle of the stream is the cleanest part.

question: A 60-year-old man on the ward is prescribed heparin by the subcutaneous route. Which technique is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to use?
option_1: Draw back the plunger to look for any blood
option_2: Give it deep into the muscle of the upper arm
option_3: Rub the site well to help the drug to spread
option_4: Give it into the abdomen and do NOT rub the site after the dose
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Give it into the abdomen and do NOT rub the site after the dose

Clinical Rationale: Heparin is given subcutaneously into the abdomen and the site is NOT rubbed, because rubbing causes bruising and bleeding.

Key Clue: heparin given by the subcutaneous route to a man

Priority Principle: Subcutaneous heparin

Why Not Others: (a) Drawing back is not done with these small doses; (b) Heparin is not given into the muscle and a muscle dose bleeds; (c) Rubbing the site causes bruising and is not done.

PGI Exam Trap: The site is rubbed after the dose to spread the drug.

5-Second Recall: Give it under the skin and do not rub.

PNC Exam Pearl: No rubbing and no muscle for heparin.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is to remove his indwelling urinary catheter. Which is the BEST order of the steps that the nurse should follow?
option_1: Explain the step, deflate the balloon, then withdraw the tube gently
option_2: Pull the tube out and then deflate the balloon
option_3: Clamp the tube for a day and then remove it
option_4: Ask the man to pull the tube out by himself
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Explain the step, deflate the balloon, then withdraw the tube gently

Clinical Rationale: The catheter is removed by explaining the step, deflating the balloon fully and then withdrawing the tube gently.

Key Clue: the removal of an indwelling urinary catheter

Priority Principle: Catheter removal

Why Not Others: (b) Withdrawing the tube with the balloon still up injures the urethra; (c) Clamping the tube for a day before removal is not the order; (d) The nurse removes the catheter and not the man himself.

PGI Exam Trap: The tube is pulled out before the balloon is deflated.

5-Second Recall: Deflate the balloon, then withdraw gently.

PNC Exam Pearl: A full balloon tears the urethra.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the unit is asked why the pulse is taken at the radial artery for a routine check. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It gives the exact blood pressure of the woman
option_2: It is the only place where the pulse can be counted
option_3: It is the strongest pulse in the whole body
option_4: It lies near the surface and is easy to feel without disturbing the woman
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) It lies near the surface and is easy to feel without disturbing the woman

Clinical Rationale: The radial artery lies close to the surface at the wrist, so the pulse is easy to feel without disturbing the woman.

Key Clue: taking the pulse at the radial artery

Priority Principle: Radial pulse

Why Not Others: (a) The pulse does not give the blood pressure by itself; (b) The pulse can also be counted at many other places; (c) The strength of the radial pulse is not the reason for choosing it.

PGI Exam Trap: The radial pulse is the only pulse that can be counted.

5-Second Recall: It is easy to feel and does not disturb the woman.

PNC Exam Pearl: The wrist is the easiest place to count the pulse.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A 45-year-old man is on the ward after an operation. Which finding is the BEST sign that he is recovering well?
option_1: He has a mild fever in the evening every day
option_2: He sleeps for MOST of the day and the night
option_3: He is hungry, sits up easily and passes urine without help
option_4: He asks for pain relief every few hours
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) He is hungry, sits up easily and passes urine without help

Clinical Rationale: A good appetite, easy movement and normal passing of urine show that the man is recovering well after the operation.

Key Clue: a 45-year-old man recovering after an operation

Priority Principle: Postoperative recovery

Why Not Others: (a) An evening fever every day points to a problem; (b) Sleeping all day is a sign of illness and not of recovery; (d) Frequent pain and the need for relief is not a sign of recovery.

PGI Exam Trap: An evening fever is taken as a sign of recovery.

5-Second Recall: Appetite, movement and urine show recovery.

PNC Exam Pearl: A recovering patient eats, moves and passes urine.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward is asked for the normal oral temperature range of a healthy adult. Which range is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: 35.0 to 36.0 degrees Celsius
option_2: 36.1 to 37.2 degrees Celsius
option_3: 37.5 to 38.5 degrees Celsius
option_4: 38.0 to 39.0 degrees Celsius
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) 36.1 to 37.2 degrees Celsius

Clinical Rationale: The normal oral temperature of a healthy adult lies between about 36.1 and 37.2 degrees Celsius.

Key Clue: the normal oral temperature range of an adult

Priority Principle: Body temperature

Why Not Others: (a) A range of 35.0 to 36.0 is below the normal range; (c) A range of 37.5 to 38.5 is a mild fever; (d) A range of 38.0 to 39.0 is a fever and not normal.

PGI Exam Trap: A range of 37.5 to 38.5 is taken as normal.

5-Second Recall: Normal oral temperature is about 36.1 to 37.2 Celsius.

PNC Exam Pearl: 36.1 to 37.2 is the normal adult range.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is to lift him up in the bed. Which action is the MOST appropriate use of body mechanics?
option_1: Keep the back straight and bend at the knees to lift
option_2: Bend the back and lift with straight legs
option_3: Twist the body while lifting the man
option_4: Hold the man away from the body while lifting
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Keep the back straight and bend at the knees to lift

Clinical Rationale: The nurse keeps the back straight and bends at the knees, so that the strong leg muscles do the work and the back is protected.

Key Clue: lifting a man up in the bed

Priority Principle: Body mechanics

Why Not Others: (b) Bending the back and lifting with straight legs strains the spine; (c) Twisting while lifting causes back injury; (d) Holding the man away from the body strains the back.

PGI Exam Trap: The man is lifted with the back bent and the legs straight.

5-Second Recall: Straight back, bent knees.

PNC Exam Pearl: The legs lift; the back stays straight.

question: A nurse caring for a family on the ward is asked about the purpose of the nursing process. Which statement is the BEST description of its purpose?
option_1: It is a record that is kept for the hospital office
option_2: It guides the nurse to plan and give care in an orderly way
option_3: It helps the nurse to finish the work more quickly
option_4: It is used when the doctor asks for a report
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) It guides the nurse to plan and give care in an orderly way

Clinical Rationale: The nursing process guides the nurse to assess, plan, give and evaluate care in an orderly and thoughtful way.

Key Clue: the purpose of the nursing process

Priority Principle: Nursing process

Why Not Others: (a) The nursing process is a way of giving care and not an office record; (c) It is not a means of finishing the work quickly; (d) It is used for every patient and not only for a report.

PGI Exam Trap: The nursing process is kept as an office record.

5-Second Recall: It plans and gives care in an orderly way.

PNC Exam Pearl: It orders the care from assessment to evaluation.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward explains why the female urethra being shorter matters during catheterisation. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The short tube means that urine is held for a long time
option_2: The short tube makes the passing of a catheter harder
option_3: The short tube lets the germs reach the bladder more easily
option_4: The short tube makes the bladder larger than the male one
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) The short tube lets the germs reach the bladder more easily

Clinical Rationale: The female urethra is short and close to the outside, so the germs reach the bladder more easily and infection is common after catheterisation.

Key Clue: the shorter female urethra and catheterisation

Priority Principle: Catheter associated infection

Why Not Others: (a) The length of the urethra does not make urine be held longer; (b) A short urethra makes the passage of a catheter easier and not harder; (d) The size of the bladder is not decided by the urethra.

PGI Exam Trap: The short urethra makes the catheter harder to pass.

5-Second Recall: A short urethra lets germs reach the bladder easily.

PNC Exam Pearl: The short female urethra invites infection.

question: A nurse caring for a family at home explains why the bag technique is essential during the home visits. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It saves the nurse the trouble of washing the hands
option_2: It helps the nurse to carry more articles to the home
option_3: It shows the family that the nurse is well trained
option_4: It keeps the articles clean and stops the transfer of infection to the home
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) It keeps the articles clean and stops the transfer of infection to the home

Clinical Rationale: The bag technique keeps the nursing articles clean and stops the transfer of infection between the homes and the nurse.

Key Clue: the bag technique during home visits

Priority Principle: Bag technique

Why Not Others: (a) Hand washing is still done and is not replaced by the bag; (b) The bag is not meant to carry a larger number of articles; (c) The technique is used for safety and not to show training.

PGI Exam Trap: The bag technique is used to save the trouble of hand washing.

5-Second Recall: It keeps the articles clean and stops infection.

PNC Exam Pearl: The clean bag keeps home and nurse safe.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the unit is to do a surgical hand wash before a sterile procedure. Which is the BEST order of the steps that the nurse should follow?
option_1: Wet, scrub up to the elbows, rinse, then dry with a sterile towel
option_2: Dry the hands FIRST, then wet and scrub them well
option_3: Scrub from the elbows down to the fingers
option_4: Scrub the hands and then dry them with a used towel
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Wet, scrub up to the elbows, rinse, then dry with a sterile towel

Clinical Rationale: A surgical hand wash wets the hands, scrubs from the fingers up to the elbows, rinses and dries with a sterile towel.

Key Clue: a surgical hand wash before a sterile procedure

Priority Principle: Surgical hand wash

Why Not Others: (b) The hands are wet before the scrub and not dried first; (c) The scrub moves from the fingers up to the elbows; (d) A used towel is not used to dry the hands after the scrub.

PGI Exam Trap: The scrub starts at the elbows and moves down to the fingers.

5-Second Recall: Wet, scrub to the elbows, rinse, dry.

PNC Exam Pearl: The scrub always moves from clean to clean.

question: A 55-year-old man on the ward has a colostomy and reports that the bag is loose and leaking. Which nursing action is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Apply a fresh bag over the old one at once
option_2: Clean the skin, dry it well and fit a bag of the correct size
option_3: Wash the area and leave the skin open to the air
option_4: Tape the loose bag to the skin around it
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Clean the skin, dry it well and fit a bag of the correct size

Clinical Rationale: The leaking bag is removed, the skin is cleaned and dried well, and a bag of the correct size is fitted so that the skin is protected.

Key Clue: a colostomy bag that is loose and leaking

Priority Principle: Colostomy care

Why Not Others: (a) A new bag over the old one does not stop the leak; (c) Leaving the skin open to the air causes soreness; (d) Taping the bag to the skin harms the skin.

PGI Exam Trap: The fresh bag is applied over the old one.

5-Second Recall: Clean and dry the skin, then fit the right bag.

PNC Exam Pearl: A dry skin and the right bag prevent the leak.

question: A nurse caring for an infant on the ward explains why infants become dehydrated quickly during a fever. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: They sweat a great deal more than older children
option_2: Their kidneys make a large amount of urine every hour
option_3: Their body surface is large for their weight and they lose more water
option_4: Their bodies hold far more water than those of adults
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Their body surface is large for their weight and they lose more water

Clinical Rationale: An infant has a large body surface for its weight, so more water is lost through the skin and the baby becomes dehydrated quickly.

Key Clue: an infant with fever who becomes dehydrated

Priority Principle: Infant dehydration

Why Not Others: (a) Sweating is not the main reason for the fast loss of water; (b) The kidneys of an infant do not make a large amount of urine; (d) An infant holds a larger share of water but loses it faster.

PGI Exam Trap: The kidneys of the infant make far more urine than an adult.

5-Second Recall: The large surface for the weight loses more water.

PNC Exam Pearl: A big surface and a small weight dry the baby fast.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for an antenatal woman in a village teaches her the danger signs of pregnancy. Which reason for this teaching is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: She can pass the information to the other families
option_2: She can treat the danger signs by herself at home
option_3: She can avoid coming to the clinic for the routine visits
option_4: She can report to the health centre early when a danger sign appears
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) She can report to the health centre early when a danger sign appears

Clinical Rationale: When the mother knows the danger signs she reports early to the health centre, so that a problem is treated before it becomes serious.

Key Clue: teaching the danger signs of pregnancy to a woman

Priority Principle: Danger signs in pregnancy

Why Not Others: (a) Passing on the information is useful but not the main reason; (b) The danger signs cannot be treated at home by the mother; (c) The teaching does not allow her to miss the routine visits.

PGI Exam Trap: The mother is taught the signs so that she can treat them herself.

5-Second Recall: Early reporting of a danger sign saves mother and baby.

PNC Exam Pearl: Know the danger sign and report early.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is to give a prescribed dose of 0.5 g of a drug. The tablets available are of 250 mg each. Which is the MOST appropriate number of tablets for the nurse to give?
option_1: Two tablets
option_2: One tablet
option_3: Half a tablet
option_4: Four tablets
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Two tablets

Clinical Rationale: A dose of 0.5 g is 500 mg, and tablets of 250 mg each means that two tablets give the prescribed dose.

Key Clue: a prescribed dose of 0.5 g with tablets of 250 mg

Priority Principle: Dose calculation

Why Not Others: (b) One tablet gives only 250 mg and half of the dose; (c) Half a tablet gives far too little of the drug; (d) Four tablets give 1000 mg and twice the dose.

PGI Exam Trap: One tablet is given for this dose.

5-Second Recall: 0.5 g equals 500 mg, so two tablets.

PNC Exam Pearl: Convert grams to milligrams before you count.

question: A nurse caring for a man who is unconscious on the ward explains why mouth care is given at regular intervals. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It keeps the mouth clean and prevents sores and infection
option_2: It wakes him up from the deep sleep
option_3: It stops him from feeling hungry between the feeds
option_4: It helps him to swallow the saliva in the mouth
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) It keeps the mouth clean and prevents sores and infection

Clinical Rationale: An unconscious patient cannot clean the mouth, so regular mouth care keeps it clean and prevents sores and infection.

Key Clue: mouth care for an unconscious man

Priority Principle: Oral care for the unconscious

Why Not Others: (b) Mouth care is not given to wake the patient from sleep; (c) Hunger between the feeds is not the reason for mouth care; (d) Mouth care does not help the swallowing of saliva.

PGI Exam Trap: Mouth care is given mainly to wake the man up.

5-Second Recall: It keeps the mouth clean and free of sores.

PNC Exam Pearl: A dry mouth breeds sores; clean it regularly.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is to give him an enema. Which position is the MOST appropriate for him?
option_1: Flat on the back with the legs straight
option_2: Left side with the knees drawn up to the abdomen
option_3: Sitting up straight in the bed
option_4: On the right side with the legs straight
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Left side with the knees drawn up to the abdomen

Clinical Rationale: For an enema the patient lies on the left side with the knees drawn up, so that the fluid flows along the natural line of the bowel.

Key Clue: the position for a man receiving an enema

Priority Principle: Enema position

Why Not Others: (a) Lying flat with the legs straight does not help the fluid to flow in; (c) Sitting up straight lets the fluid run out at once; (d) The right side is not the position used for an enema.

PGI Exam Trap: The patient lies on the right side for an enema.

5-Second Recall: Left side with the knees drawn up.

PNC Exam Pearl: Left side follows the line of the bowel.

question: A 70-year-old man on the ward has an intravenous cannula and the nurse finds redness and pus at the site. Which action is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Apply a warm pack over the cannula site
option_2: Clean the site and leave the cannula in place
option_3: Remove the cannula and send the tip for culture
option_4: Flush the cannula well with saline
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Remove the cannula and send the tip for culture

Clinical Rationale: Redness and pus at a cannula site mean an infection, so the cannula is removed at once and the tip is sent for culture.

Key Clue: redness and pus at the intravenous cannula site

Priority Principle: Cannula site infection

Why Not Others: (a) A warm pack does not treat the infection at the site; (b) A cannula that is infected must not be left in place; (d) Flushing pushes the germs into the blood stream.

PGI Exam Trap: The cannula is cleaned and left in place.

5-Second Recall: Remove the cannula and culture the tip.

PNC Exam Pearl: An infected cannula comes out at once.

question: A woman on the ward after a caesarean birth has abdominal distension with no bowel sounds on the second day. Which condition is the MOST likely?
option_1: Deep vein thrombosis
option_2: Wound infection
option_3: Urinary retention
option_4: Paralytic ileus
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Paralytic ileus

Clinical Rationale: A distended abdomen with absent bowel sounds after surgery points to a paralytic ileus, in which the bowel movement stops.

Key Clue: abdominal distension with no bowel sounds after a caesarean

Priority Principle: Paralytic ileus

Why Not Others: (a) A deep vein thrombosis gives calf pain and swelling; (b) A wound infection gives fever and discharge at the wound; (c) Urinary retention gives a full bladder and not a silent abdomen.

PGI Exam Trap: The silent abdomen is read as a wound infection.

5-Second Recall: A silent, distended abdomen means ileus.

PNC Exam Pearl: No bowel sounds means the bowel has stopped.

question: A nurse caring for a family in a village explains why intersectoral coordination is important in the community health programmes. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It keeps the other departments away from health matters
option_2: It reduces the number of staff needed for the health work
option_3: It gives the health department more money for its work
option_4: Health needs are met better when the health and other sectors plan together
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Health needs are met better when the health and other sectors plan together

Clinical Rationale: Health depends on water, food, education and other sectors, so the needs of the people are met better when the sectors plan together.

Key Clue: intersectoral coordination in community health programmes

Priority Principle: Intersectoral coordination

Why Not Others: (a) Coordination brings the other sectors in and not away; (b) The aim is not to reduce the number of health staff; (c) Extra money for the department is not the reason for coordination.

PGI Exam Trap: The purpose is to get more money for the health department.

5-Second Recall: Sectors together meet the health needs better.

PNC Exam Pearl: Health is built by many sectors together.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward reads a urine culture report that shows more than one lakh colonies of a single organism per millilitre. Which interpretation is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It is a normal report and needs no action
option_2: It shows that the sample was badly contaminated
option_3: It confirms a urinary tract infection in this woman
option_4: It means that the woman has a kidney stone
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) It confirms a urinary tract infection in this woman

Clinical Rationale: A growth of more than one lakh colonies of a single organism in a millilitre of urine confirms a urinary tract infection.

Key Clue: more than one lakh colonies of a single organism in urine

Priority Principle: Urine culture

Why Not Others: (a) Such a growth is not a normal report; (b) A single organism in large numbers means infection and not contamination; (d) The culture does not show a kidney stone.

PGI Exam Trap: A single organism in large numbers is taken as contamination.

5-Second Recall: A single organism in lakhs means infection.

PNC Exam Pearl: One germ in lakhs is a real infection.

question: A nurse caring for a family in a village notes that the village has a population of 6000 people and 80 deaths in a year. Which is the MOST appropriate crude death rate?
option_1: 8.0 per 1000 population
option_2: 13.3 per 1000 population
option_3: 18.0 per 1000 population
option_4: 6.0 per 1000 population
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) 13.3 per 1000 population

Clinical Rationale: The crude death rate is the deaths in a year for every 1000 people, so 80 deaths among 6000 people gives about 13.3.

Key Clue: a population of 6000 and 80 deaths in a year

Priority Principle: Crude death rate

Why Not Others: (a) A figure of 8.0 is too low for these numbers; (c) A figure of 18.0 is too high for these numbers; (d) A figure of 6.0 is far too low for these numbers.

PGI Exam Trap: The deaths are divided by ten to get the rate.

5-Second Recall: Deaths per 1000 people in a year.

PNC Exam Pearl: Divide the deaths and multiply by a thousand.

question: A nurse caring for a family in a village explains why the family is taken as the unit of service in community health nursing. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The health of one member is linked with the health of the whole family
option_2: Every family in the village has the same health problems
option_3: It is easier to visit a family than to visit a person
option_4: The family pays for the services given by the nurse
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) The health of one member is linked with the health of the whole family

Clinical Rationale: The health of one member affects and is affected by the other members, so the family is taken as the unit of service.

Key Clue: the family as the unit of service in community health nursing

Priority Principle: Family as unit of care

Why Not Others: (b) Families differ in their health problems and are not all the same; (c) The choice is based on health and not on ease of visiting; (d) The family does not pay for the services of the nurse.

PGI Exam Trap: The family is chosen because every family is alike.

5-Second Recall: One member's health is tied to the family's health.

PNC Exam Pearl: Treat the family to treat the person.

question: A nurse caring for a man on antibiotics explains why a broad spectrum antibiotic is given with care and only when it is needed. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It must be given by the intravenous route
option_2: It is much more costly than the other antibiotics
option_3: It acts more slowly than the narrow spectrum drugs
option_4: It kills the useful bacteria too and lets resistant germs grow
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) It kills the useful bacteria too and lets resistant germs grow

Clinical Rationale: A broad spectrum drug kills the useful bacteria of the body as well, so resistant germs get a chance to grow and the drug is used with care.

Key Clue: the careful use of a broad spectrum antibiotic

Priority Principle: Antibiotic use

Why Not Others: (a) Broad spectrum drugs are also given by mouth and not only into the vein; (b) The cost is a small matter and not the reason for the care; (c) These drugs are not slower than the narrow spectrum drugs.

PGI Exam Trap: The drug is restricted mainly because it costs more.

5-Second Recall: It harms the useful bacteria and breeds resistance.

PNC Exam Pearl: Wide killing means wider resistance.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward is to apply a hot water bag to relieve her pain. Which is the BEST order of the steps that the nurse should follow?
option_1: Check the skin, fill and cover the bag, then apply it for a short time
option_2: Fill the bag with boiling water and apply it at once
option_3: Apply the bag directly on the skin for a long time
option_4: Fill the bag and leave it on the bed for the woman
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Check the skin, fill and cover the bag, then apply it for a short time

Clinical Rationale: The skin is checked FIRST, the bag is filled and covered, and it is then applied for a short time so that the skin is NOT burnt.

Key Clue: applying a hot water bag to relieve pain

Priority Principle: Hot water bag

Why Not Others: (b) Boiling water in the bag burns the skin of the woman; (c) The bag is never put directly on the skin; (d) The bag is applied by the nurse and not left on the bed.

PGI Exam Trap: The bag is filled with boiling water and applied at once.

5-Second Recall: Check the skin, cover the bag, apply briefly.

PNC Exam Pearl: Cover the bag and watch the skin.

question: A 58-year-old man on the ward who takes insulin reports trembling, sweating and dizziness just before lunch. Which action is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to take?
option_1: Give him his next dose of insulin early
option_2: Give him a glucose drink or a sweet at once
option_3: Ask him to lie down and rest till the meal
option_4: Give him a glass of water and wait for lunch
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Give him a glucose drink or a sweet at once

Clinical Rationale: Trembling, sweating and dizziness before a meal point to low blood sugar, so a glucose drink or a sweet is given at once.

Key Clue: trembling, sweating and dizziness in a man on insulin

Priority Principle: Hypoglycaemia

Why Not Others: (a) More insulin lowers the sugar further and is dangerous; (c) Resting does not raise the blood sugar; (d) Waiting for lunch leaves the low sugar untreated.

PGI Exam Trap: The next dose of insulin is given early to settle him.

5-Second Recall: Give sugar at once for the low blood sugar.

PNC Exam Pearl: Sweating and trembling mean sugar, not insulin.

question: A nurse caring for a family on the ward explains why hand hygiene is called the single MOST important measure of infection control. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It is the method that is taught FIRST to nursing students
option_2: It is the cheapest of all the methods of infection control
option_3: The hands carry germs from one person to another and clean hands stop this
option_4: It kills all the germs that are present in the hospital
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) The hands carry germs from one person to another and clean hands stop this

Clinical Rationale: The hands carry the germs from one patient to another, so clean hands break this chain and prevent MOST hospital infections.

Key Clue: the importance of hand hygiene in infection control

Priority Principle: Hand hygiene

Why Not Others: (a) Being taught first does not make it the most important; (b) Low cost is a benefit and not the reason for its importance; (d) Hand hygiene reduces the germs and does not kill them all.

PGI Exam Trap: Hand hygiene is the BEST method mainly because it is cheap.

5-Second Recall: Clean hands break the chain of infection.

PNC Exam Pearl: Clean hands carry no germs to the next patient.

question: A nurse caring for a man with kidney failure explains why the dose of many drugs is reduced for him. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The man needs much less of every medicine
option_2: The drug is absorbed better in the failing kidney
option_3: The kidneys cannot clear the drug, so it builds up in the body
option_4: The drug is destroyed faster by the failing kidney
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) The kidneys cannot clear the drug, so it builds up in the body

Clinical Rationale: The kidneys clear MOST drugs from the body, so when they fail the drug stays in the blood and its dose is reduced.

Key Clue: the dose of a drug in a man with kidney failure

Priority Principle: Drugs in renal failure

Why Not Others: (a) The man does not need less of every medicine; (b) The failing kidney does not absorb the drug better; (d) The failing kidney destroys the drug more slowly and not faster.

PGI Exam Trap: The drug is destroyed faster when the kidney fails.

5-Second Recall: A failing kidney cannot clear the drug.

PNC Exam Pearl: No clearance means a smaller dose.

question: A nurse caring for a woman in labour reads the partograph, which shows the cervix dilated 4 cm at 9 am and still 4 cm at 1 pm. Which interpretation is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The labour is progressing normally for this stage
option_2: The labour has NOT progressed and needs urgent review
option_3: The partograph has been filled in wrongly
option_4: The woman will deliver very soon now
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) The labour has NOT progressed and needs urgent review

Clinical Rationale: The cervix should open with time in the active phase, so no opening in four hours means that the labour has stopped progressing and needs urgent review.

Key Clue: the cervix dilated 4 cm at 9 am and 4 cm at 1 pm

Priority Principle: Partograph interpretation

Why Not Others: (a) No progress in four hours is not normal for the active phase; (c) The finding is a real one and the chart is not wrong; (d) A woman with no progress will not deliver very soon.

PGI Exam Trap: No progress in four hours is taken as normal.

5-Second Recall: A still cervix needs an urgent review.

PNC Exam Pearl: The partograph shows slow labour early.

question: A nurse caring for a 2-year-old child with moderate dehydration is giving oral rehydration fluid, and the child vomits once. Which action is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Wait a short while, then give the fluid again in small sips
option_2: Stop the oral fluid and start an intravenous line
option_3: Give a large amount of the fluid at once to make up
option_4: Stop all fluids and review the child after an hour
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Wait a short while, then give the fluid again in small sips

Clinical Rationale: A single vomit does NOT stop oral rehydration, so the nurse waits a short while and then gives the fluid again in small sips.

Key Clue: a 2-year-old child on oral rehydration who vomits once

Priority Principle: Oral rehydration therapy

Why Not Others: (b) An intravenous line is not needed after a single vomit; (c) A large amount at once makes the child vomit again; (d) Stopping the fluids lets the dehydration become worse.

PGI Exam Trap: The oral fluid is stopped after a single vomit.

5-Second Recall: Wait, then give small sips again.

PNC Exam Pearl: Small sips stay down better than a large volume.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward reads his intake and output chart, which shows an intake of 2500 ml and a urine output of 600 ml in twenty four hours. Which interpretation is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The chart shows that the kidneys are working very well
option_2: The chart is normal and the man needs no review
option_3: The output is low because the man is NOT drinking enough
option_4: The output is far less than the intake and must be reported at once
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) The output is far less than the intake and must be reported at once

Clinical Rationale: A urine output of 600 ml against an intake of 2500 ml in a day is far less than it should be, so the nurse reports it at once.

Key Clue: an intake of 2500 ml and a urine output of 600 ml

Priority Principle: Intake and output chart

Why Not Others: (a) A small output means the kidneys are not working well; (b) Such a wide gap between the intake and the output is not normal; (c) The man has taken 2500 ml and so is drinking well.

PGI Exam Trap: The chart is read as a sign of good kidney function.

5-Second Recall: The output is too low against the intake; report it.

PNC Exam Pearl: Watch the gap between intake and output.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward is asked which route of drug administration gives the fastest onset of action. Which route is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The intramuscular route
option_2: The oral route
option_3: The intravenous route
option_4: The subcutaneous route
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) The intravenous route

Clinical Rationale: A drug given into the vein enters the blood at once and gives the fastest onset of action of all the routes.

Key Clue: the route of drug administration with the fastest onset

Priority Principle: Routes of administration

Why Not Others: (a) The intramuscular route is faster than the oral route but slower than the vein; (b) The oral route is slow because the drug must be taken in and absorbed; (d) The subcutaneous route is slower than the intramuscular route.

PGI Exam Trap: The oral route acts faster than the intravenous route.

5-Second Recall: The intravenous route acts fastest of all.

PNC Exam Pearl: Into the vein means into the blood at once.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward explains why the correct position matters after an intramuscular injection into the ventrogluteal site. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It keeps the man from moving during the injection
option_2: It makes the injection less painful for the man
option_3: It helps the drug to act much more quickly
option_4: It helps the nurse to find the safe site and avoid the nerves and vessels
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) It helps the nurse to find the safe site and avoid the nerves and vessels

Clinical Rationale: The correct position brings the ventrogluteal site into view and keeps the needle away from the nerves and the blood vessels.

Key Clue: the position for an intramuscular injection into the ventrogluteal site

Priority Principle: Intramuscular injection

Why Not Others: (a) Stillness helps but the safe site is the real reason; (b) Comfort is a benefit and not the reason for the position; (c) The onset of the drug does not depend on this position.

PGI Exam Trap: The position is chosen to make the injection less painful.

5-Second Recall: The right position finds the safe site.

PNC Exam Pearl: A good position keeps the nerve away.

question: A nurse caring for a helpless man on the ward is to give him a bed bath. Which is the BEST order of the steps that the nurse should follow?
option_1: Explain, wash the face, then the body, then the back and perineum
option_2: Wash the perineum FIRST and then the face
option_3: Wash the back FIRST and leave the face for the end
option_4: Give the bath without telling the man about it
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Explain, wash the face, then the body, then the back and perineum

Clinical Rationale: A bed bath begins with an explanation, then the face is washed, then the body, and the back and perineum are washed last.

Key Clue: the bed bath of a helpless man

Priority Principle: Bed bath

Why Not Others: (b) The perineum is washed last because it is the dirtiest area; (c) The face is washed first and not left for the end; (d) The patient is always told about the bath before it is given.

PGI Exam Trap: The perineum is washed before the face.

5-Second Recall: Explain, then face, body, back and perineum.

PNC Exam Pearl: Wash from the cleanest to the dirtiest.

question: A nurse caring for a family on the ward is asked about the evaluation step of the nursing process. Which statement is the BEST description of this step?
option_1: It writes down the plan of the care in the file
option_2: It checks whether the goals of the care have been met
option_3: It collects the FIRST information about the patient
option_4: It gives the medicines that the doctor ordered
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) It checks whether the goals of the care have been met

Clinical Rationale: Evaluation is the last step of the nursing process, in which the nurse checks whether the goals of the care have been met.

Key Clue: the evaluation step of the nursing process

Priority Principle: Nursing process

Why Not Others: (a) Writing the plan is a part of the planning step and not evaluation; (c) Collecting the first information is the assessment step; (d) Giving the medicines is the implementation of the plan.

PGI Exam Trap: The FIRST information is collected during evaluation.

5-Second Recall: Evaluation checks whether the goals were met.

PNC Exam Pearl: Evaluation looks back at the goals.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which drug group needs the closest monitoring of the apical pulse before every dose. Which group is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The analgesic group of drugs
option_2: The diuretic group of drugs
option_3: The antibiotic group of drugs
option_4: The digitalis group of drugs
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) The digitalis group of drugs

Clinical Rationale: Digitalis slows and strengthens the heart, so the apical pulse is checked before every dose to avoid a dangerously slow rate.

Key Clue: the drug group needing an apical pulse check before each dose

Priority Principle: Digitalis drugs

Why Not Others: (a) Analgesics need no apical pulse check before the dose; (b) Diuretics need a check of the weight and the potassium and not the apical pulse; (c) Antibiotics need no apical pulse check before the dose.

PGI Exam Trap: The diuretics need an apical pulse check before each dose.

5-Second Recall: Digitalis drugs slow the pulse and are checked.

PNC Exam Pearl: With digitalis, count the pulse before the dose.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is to change the sterile dressing over his wound. Which is the BEST order of the steps that the nurse should follow?
option_1: Apply the new dressing and then remove the old one
option_2: Clean the wound from the outside towards the middle
option_3: Explain, remove the old dressing, clean from clean to dirty, then apply
option_4: Clean the wound with the same swab again and again
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Explain, remove the old dressing, clean from clean to dirty, then apply

Clinical Rationale: A sterile dressing change explains the step, removes the old dressing, cleans from the clean area outward, and then applies the new dressing.

Key Clue: changing the sterile dressing over a wound

Priority Principle: Sterile dressing

Why Not Others: (a) The old dressing is removed before the new one is applied; (b) The wound is cleaned from the middle outwards and not from the outside in; (d) A used swab is not used again on the wound.

PGI Exam Trap: The wound is cleaned from the outside towards the middle.

5-Second Recall: Clean from the centre outwards.

PNC Exam Pearl: Clean to dirty, never dirty to clean.

question: A man on the ward after an operation is on a clear fluid diet and asks for a cup of milk. Which response by the nurse is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Give the milk because it is a fluid and he is thirsty
option_2: Explain that milk is NOT a clear fluid and offer him clear soup instead
option_3: Refuse the milk and give him nothing at all
option_4: Give the milk and reduce the other fluids for the day
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Explain that milk is NOT a clear fluid and offer him clear soup instead

Clinical Rationale: Milk is NOT a clear fluid, so the nurse explains this and offers a clear fluid such as soup instead of refusing the request outright.

Key Clue: a postoperative man on a clear fluid diet asking for milk

Priority Principle: Clear fluid diet

Why Not Others: (a) Milk is not clear and is not allowed on this diet; (c) Giving nothing is unkind; a clear fluid can be offered; (d) The other fluids are not cut down to allow the milk.

PGI Exam Trap: Milk is given as a clear fluid on this diet.

5-Second Recall: Explain and offer a clear fluid instead.

PNC Exam Pearl: Milk is not clear; soup is.

question: A man on the ward who is on bed rest complains of pain in the calf with swelling of one leg. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Keep the leg still, do NOT rub it, and inform the doctor at once
option_2: Massage the calf well to relieve the pain
option_3: Ask him to walk about to improve the blood flow
option_4: Apply a warm pack on the calf and watch it
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Keep the leg still, do NOT rub it, and inform the doctor at once

Clinical Rationale: Calf pain with swelling in a man on bed rest suggests a clot, so the leg is kept still, is NOT rubbed, and the doctor is told at once.

Key Clue: calf pain with swelling of one leg in a man on bed rest

Priority Principle: Deep vein thrombosis

Why Not Others: (b) Massaging may loosen the clot and send it to the lungs; (c) Walking about may loosen the clot and is dangerous; (d) A warm pack does not treat the clot and delays the report.

PGI Exam Trap: The calf is massaged well to ease the pain.

5-Second Recall: Keep the leg still and call the doctor.

PNC Exam Pearl: A painful swollen calf is not to be rubbed.

question: A nurse caring for an agitated man on the unit explains why a quiet place with few stimuli is given to him. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: A quiet place keeps him away from the other patients
option_2: Too much noise and activity make him more restless and upset
option_3: It helps the staff to finish the ward work quickly
option_4: It is the rule of the hospital for such patients
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Too much noise and activity make him more restless and upset

Clinical Rationale: An agitated patient cannot screen out noise and movement, so a quiet place with few stimuli helps him to settle and become less restless.

Key Clue: a quiet place with few stimuli for an agitated man

Priority Principle: Care of the agitated patient

Why Not Others: (a) The aim is to settle him and not to keep him away from others; (c) The comfort of the patient and not the ward work is the aim; (d) The practice is based on care and not on a hospital rule.

PGI Exam Trap: The quiet place is given to keep him from the other patients.

5-Second Recall: Less noise means less restlessness.

PNC Exam Pearl: Fewer stimuli calm an agitated mind.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward explains why the pH of the aspirate is checked before a feed through the nasogastric tube. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It shows that the tube is in the stomach and NOT in the lung
option_2: It tells how much feed the man will need
option_3: It shows whether the feed is at the right temperature
option_4: It tells whether the tube is blocked or NOT
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) It shows that the tube is in the stomach and NOT in the lung

Clinical Rationale: The aspirate from the stomach is acidic, so its pH shows that the tube lies in the stomach and NOT in the airway.

Key Clue: the pH of the aspirate before a nasogastric feed

Priority Principle: Nasogastric tube position

Why Not Others: (b) The pH does not tell the amount of feed that is needed; (c) The temperature of the feed is a separate check; (d) A blocked tube is found by other means and not by the pH.

PGI Exam Trap: The pH tells the amount of feed that the man needs.

5-Second Recall: An acid pH shows the tube is in the stomach.

PNC Exam Pearl: Acid aspirate means the stomach.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked for the correct definition of the apical pulse. Which statement is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The pulse that is counted during the sleep of the patient
option_2: The beat felt at the wrist for half a minute
option_3: The beat counted for fifteen seconds and doubled
option_4: The beat heard over the heart with a stethoscope for one minute
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) The beat heard over the heart with a stethoscope for one minute

Clinical Rationale: The apical pulse is the beat of the heart heard over the apex with a stethoscope and counted for a full minute.

Key Clue: the definition of the apical pulse

Priority Principle: Apical pulse

Why Not Others: (a) Counting during sleep describes when the pulse is taken and not what it is; (b) The pulse felt at the wrist is the radial pulse and not the apical; (c) A fifteen second count gives the rate and not the definition.

PGI Exam Trap: The pulse at the wrist is called the apical pulse.

5-Second Recall: The apical pulse is heard over the heart.

PNC Exam Pearl: The apical pulse is a listened pulse.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which finding is the MOST appropriate early sign of hypoxia in an adult.
option_1: A very slow pulse rate
option_2: A bluish colour of the lips
option_3: Restlessness and poor concentration
option_4: A fall in the body temperature
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Restlessness and poor concentration

Clinical Rationale: Restlessness and poor concentration appear early when the brain is short of oxygen, before the later signs such as blue lips.

Key Clue: the early sign of hypoxia in an adult

Priority Principle: Hypoxia

Why Not Others: (a) The pulse usually becomes fast and not very slow; (b) Blue lips appear later when the hypoxia is more severe; (d) The temperature does not fall as an early sign of hypoxia.

PGI Exam Trap: Blue lips are the earliest sign of hypoxia.

5-Second Recall: Restlessness is the earliest sign.

PNC Exam Pearl: The brain complains first when oxygen is low.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the unit is asked which statement about informed consent before a procedure is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: The consent is signed by the nurse on behalf of the woman
option_2: The woman must understand the procedure and agree to it freely
option_3: The consent can be taken after the procedure is done
option_4: A verbal consent from the family is enough for surgery
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) The woman must understand the procedure and agree to it freely

Clinical Rationale: Informed consent means that the woman understands the procedure and agrees to it on her own, without pressure from anyone.

Key Clue: informed consent before a procedure

Priority Principle: Informed consent

Why Not Others: (a) The nurse does not sign the consent for the woman; (c) The consent is taken before and not after the procedure; (d) Surgery needs the written consent of the woman herself.

PGI Exam Trap: The nurse signs the consent on behalf of the woman.

5-Second Recall: She understands it and agrees freely.

PNC Exam Pearl: Consent must be informed and free.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is to give 1.5 litres of fluid in twenty four hours at a rate of 30 ml per hour. Which is the MOST appropriate number of hours for the infusion to take?
option_1: 50 hours
option_2: 30 hours
option_3: 45 hours
option_4: 60 hours
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) 50 hours

Clinical Rationale: A volume of 1.5 litres is 1500 ml, and at 30 ml in an hour the infusion takes 1500 divided by 30, which is 50 hours.

Key Clue: 1500 ml to be given at 30 ml per hour

Priority Principle: Infusion time

Why Not Others: (b) Thirty hours gives only 900 ml of the fluid; (c) Forty five hours gives only 1350 ml of the fluid; (d) Sixty hours gives 1800 ml and more than the order.

PGI Exam Trap: Thirty hours is enough for the whole 1500 ml.

5-Second Recall: Divide the volume by the hourly rate.

PNC Exam Pearl: Time equals volume divided by the rate.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward reads a blood sugar report of 180 mg per decilitre taken two hours after a meal. Which interpretation is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The level is normal when the man is fasting
option_2: The level is normal for a person after a meal
option_3: The level shows a very low blood sugar
option_4: The level is higher than the target for two hours after a meal
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) The level is higher than the target for two hours after a meal

Clinical Rationale: Two hours after a meal the blood sugar should be well under 180 mg per decilitre, so this reading is higher than the target.

Key Clue: a blood sugar of 180 mg per decilitre after a meal

Priority Principle: Blood sugar report

Why Not Others: (a) A fasting level of 180 would be even more abnormal; (b) A level of 180 after a meal is above the usual target; (c) A very low sugar gives a reading far below this figure.

PGI Exam Trap: A level of 180 after a meal is taken as normal.

5-Second Recall: The reading is above the two hour target.

PNC Exam Pearl: After a meal the sugar should be lower than this.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is to give a drug three times a day, and the FIRST dose is due at 8 am. Which schedule is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: 8 am, 8 pm and midnight of the day
option_2: 8 am, 12 noon and 4 pm in the day
option_3: 8 am, 2 pm and 8 pm at even intervals in the day
option_4: 8 am and 8 pm twice in the day
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) 8 am, 2 pm and 8 pm at even intervals in the day

Clinical Rationale: A drug given three times a day is spaced evenly through the waking hours, such as 8 am, 2 pm and 8 pm.

Key Clue: a drug prescribed three times a day with the FIRST dose at 8 am

Priority Principle: Dose schedule

Why Not Others: (a) Midnight is not used in the usual three times a day schedule; (b) Noon and 4 pm crowd the doses into the morning and leave a long night gap; (d) Twice a day gives only two doses and not the three ordered.

PGI Exam Trap: The drug is given twice a day for the order of three times.

5-Second Recall: Space the three doses evenly through the day.

PNC Exam Pearl: Three times a day means an even spread.

question: A nurse caring for a family on the ward is asked about the concept of holistic nursing care. Which statement is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It cares for the body, the mind and the social needs of the person
option_2: It cares for the disease that the person has
option_3: It treats each patient exactly in the same way
option_4: It gives care to the family and NOT to the patient
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) It cares for the body, the mind and the social needs of the person

Clinical Rationale: Holistic care treats the person as a whole, so the body, the mind and the social needs are all cared for together.

Key Clue: the concept of holistic nursing care

Priority Principle: Holistic care

Why Not Others: (b) Care of the disease alone is not holistic care; (c) Holistic care is planned for each person and not given in the same way to all; (d) The family is included but the patient remains the centre of care.

PGI Exam Trap: Holistic care treats every patient in the same way.

5-Second Recall: It cares for the whole person, not just the disease.

PNC Exam Pearl: Treat the person, not only the illness.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the unit explains why autoclaving is preferred over boiling for the sterilisation of surgical instruments. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Boiling is a much slower method of sterilisation
option_2: Steam under pressure kills the spores as well as the germs
option_3: Autoclaving uses less water than the boiling method
option_4: Boiling damages the sharp edges of the instruments
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Steam under pressure kills the spores as well as the germs

Clinical Rationale: Autoclaving uses steam under pressure, which kills the resistant spores as well, while boiling does NOT kill all the spores.

Key Clue: autoclaving compared with boiling for instruments

Priority Principle: Sterilisation

Why Not Others: (a) The advantage is not the speed but the killing of the spores; (c) The amount of water used is not the reason; (d) Boiling does not damage the edges to this extent.

PGI Exam Trap: Autoclaving is preferred mainly because it is quicker.

5-Second Recall: Steam under pressure kills the spores too.

PNC Exam Pearl: Spores survive boiling but not the autoclave.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked about the layers of the skin from the surface inwards, which matters for wound care. Which order is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Subcutaneous layer, dermis, then the epidermis
option_2: Dermis, epidermis, then the subcutaneous layer
option_3: Epidermis, dermis, then the subcutaneous layer
option_4: Epidermis, subcutaneous layer, then the dermis
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Epidermis, dermis, then the subcutaneous layer

Clinical Rationale: From the surface inwards the skin is made of the epidermis, then the dermis, and then the subcutaneous layer.

Key Clue: the layers of the skin from the surface inwards

Priority Principle: Skin layers

Why Not Others: (a) The subcutaneous layer is the deepest and not the first; (b) The dermis lies under the epidermis and not above it; (d) The subcutaneous layer lies below the dermis and not above it.

PGI Exam Trap: The dermis is the outermost layer of the skin.

5-Second Recall: Epidermis, then dermis, then subcutaneous.

PNC Exam Pearl: Epidermis on top, dermis below.

question: A 65-year-old man on the ward who takes warfarin reports bleeding gums and dark stools. Which action is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Ask him to eat more green vegetables each day
option_2: Give the next dose of warfarin on time as ordered
option_3: Advise him to use a softer toothbrush from now
option_4: Hold the next dose, check the clotting report and inform the doctor
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Hold the next dose, check the clotting report and inform the doctor

Clinical Rationale: Bleeding gums and dark stools are signs of too much warfarin, so the next dose is held, the clotting is checked and the doctor is told.

Key Clue: bleeding gums and dark stools in a man on warfarin

Priority Principle: Warfarin overdose

Why Not Others: (a) Green vegetables change the action of warfarin and are not the first step; (b) Another dose of warfarin makes the bleeding worse; (c) A softer brush is a small step and misses the serious bleeding.

PGI Exam Trap: The next dose of warfarin is given on time as ordered.

5-Second Recall: Hold the dose and check the clotting.

PNC Exam Pearl: Bleeding on warfarin means check the clotting.
