question: A nurse caring for a depressed woman on the unit sees that the risk of self harm is recorded as high. Which nursing action is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Move her to a room far from the nurse station
option_2: Leave her alone so that she can rest quietly
option_3: Ask the family to stay away for some days
option_4: Keep her under close observation and remove harmful objects
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Keep her under close observation and remove harmful objects

Clinical Rationale: A high risk of self harm needs close observation, and any object that could be used for harm is removed from her reach.

Key Clue: a depressed woman with a high risk of self harm

Priority Principle: Risk of self harm

Why Not Others: (a) A room far from the nurses makes observation harder; (b) Leaving her alone is unsafe when the risk is high; (c) Keeping the family away takes away her support.

PGI Exam Trap: She is left alone to rest quietly in her room.

5-Second Recall: Watch her closely and take away sharp objects.

PNC Exam Pearl: High risk means close watch.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward keeps all her health information confidential. Which is the MOST appropriate principle of ethics that the nurse is following here?
option_1: The principle of confidentiality
option_2: The principle of autonomy
option_3: The principle of justice
option_4: The principle of beneficence
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) The principle of confidentiality

Clinical Rationale: Keeping the health information of a patient private is the ethical principle of confidentiality.

Key Clue: keeping the health information of a patient private

Priority Principle: Ethical principles

Why Not Others: (b) Autonomy is the right of the patient to decide about her own care; (c) Justice means fair treatment for all the patients; (d) Beneficence means doing good for the patient.

PGI Exam Trap: Keeping the information private is called autonomy.

5-Second Recall: Private information follows confidentiality.

PNC Exam Pearl: Confidentiality guards the record.

question: A nurse caring for a man after uncomplicated surgery explains why early walking about is encouraged. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It helps the man to leave the hospital on the same day
option_2: It improves the circulation and prevents clots and chest problems
option_3: It keeps the man from asking for pain relief
option_4: It reduces the work of the nurses on the ward
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) It improves the circulation and prevents clots and chest problems

Clinical Rationale: Walking about early after surgery keeps the blood moving and the chest clear, so clots and chest problems are prevented.

Key Clue: early walking about after uncomplicated surgery

Priority Principle: Early ambulation

Why Not Others: (a) Early walking does not mean that he leaves the same day; (c) Walking about is not a way of avoiding pain relief; (d) The aim is the man's health and not less work for the nurses.

PGI Exam Trap: Early walking is encouraged to reduce the work of the nurses.

5-Second Recall: It keeps the blood moving and the chest clear.

PNC Exam Pearl: Movement prevents clots; deep breathing clears the chest.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward explains why the patient is identified with two identifiers before every procedure. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It helps the nurse to remember the name of the patient
option_2: It follows the rule of the hospital and nothing more
option_3: Two identifiers stop a mistake when two patients have the same name
option_4: It shows the patient that the nurse is well trained
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Two identifiers stop a mistake when two patients have the same name

Clinical Rationale: Two identifiers such as the name and the hospital number stop a mix up when two patients share the same name.

Key Clue: identifying a patient with two identifiers before a procedure

Priority Principle: Patient identification

Why Not Others: (a) Remembering the name is not the purpose of the check; (b) The practice is based on safety and not on a rule alone; (d) The check is for the safety of the patient and not for show.

PGI Exam Trap: Two identifiers are used mainly to show the training of the nurse.

5-Second Recall: Two identifiers prevent a mix up of patients.

PNC Exam Pearl: Two checks catch the one that slips.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is to change his ostomy bag. Which is the BEST order of the steps that the nurse should follow?
option_1: Empty the bag, remove it, clean and dry the skin, then fit a new one
option_2: Fit the new bag FIRST and then remove the old one from the skin
option_3: Clean the stoma with spirit and leave the skin wet before the bag
option_4: Remove the bag and leave the stoma open to the air for a while
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Empty the bag, remove it, clean and dry the skin, then fit a new one

Clinical Rationale: An ostomy bag is changed by emptying it, removing it, cleaning and drying the skin, and then fitting a new bag of the right size.

Key Clue: changing the ostomy bag of a man

Priority Principle: Ostomy care

Why Not Others: (b) The new bag cannot be fitted before the old one is removed; (c) Spirit is too harsh and a wet skin will not hold the bag; (d) Leaving the stoma open to the air causes soreness.

PGI Exam Trap: The new bag is fitted before the old one is removed.

5-Second Recall: Empty, remove, clean and dry, then fit.

PNC Exam Pearl: A dry skin holds the new bag.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is to give 1 unit of packed cells over four hours. One unit is 350 ml. Which is the MOST appropriate volume to be given each hour?
option_1: About 60 ml each hour
option_2: About 70 ml each hour
option_3: About 100 ml each hour
option_4: About 88 ml each hour
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) About 88 ml each hour

Clinical Rationale: A unit of 350 ml given over four hours works out at about 88 ml in each hour of the transfusion.

Key Clue: 350 ml of packed cells to be given over four hours

Priority Principle: Blood transfusion rate

Why Not Others: (a) Sixty in an hour is too slow and gives only 240 ml; (b) Seventy in an hour gives only 280 ml in four hours; (c) A hundred in an hour gives 400 ml and more than one unit.

PGI Exam Trap: The unit is divided by six to get the hourly rate.

5-Second Recall: Divide the volume by the hours.

PNC Exam Pearl: Volume over time gives the rate.

question: A nurse caring for a man who lies supine on the ward for a long time places a pillow under his thighs. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It helps the man to breathe more easily
option_2: It keeps the man warm during the long rest
option_3: It reduces the pull on the back and keeps the heels off the bed
option_4: It stops the man from turning in the bed
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) It reduces the pull on the back and keeps the heels off the bed

Clinical Rationale: A pillow under the thighs slightly bends the knees, which reduces the pull on the lower back and keeps the heels from pressing on the bed.

Key Clue: a pillow under the thighs of a man lying supine

Priority Principle: Correct positioning

Why Not Others: (a) Breathing is helped by raising the head and not by this pillow; (b) Warmth is not the reason for the pillow; (d) The pillow does not stop him from turning.

PGI Exam Trap: The pillow is placed to keep the man warm.

5-Second Recall: It eases the back and lifts the heels.

PNC Exam Pearl: Bent knees take the strain off the back.

question: A nurse caring for a family in a village explains why the records and reports of the sub centre are maintained. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: They are kept to fill the shelves of the sub centre
option_2: They give the facts needed to plan care and to continue it properly
option_3: They are needed to find fault with the staff of the centre
option_4: They are sent to the office once in a year
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) They give the facts needed to plan care and to continue it properly

Clinical Rationale: The records and reports of the sub centre give the facts about the people and the care, which are needed to plan and continue the work.

Key Clue: the records and reports of a sub centre

Priority Principle: Records and reports

Why Not Others: (a) The records are kept for the care and not to fill the shelves; (c) The purpose is planning and not finding fault with the staff; (d) The reports are sent at set intervals and not only once a year.

PGI Exam Trap: The records are kept only to fill the shelves of the centre.

5-Second Recall: Records give the facts for planning care.

PNC Exam Pearl: Good records plan good care.

question: A man on the ward has a nasogastric tube and now has a distended abdomen with no aspirate on checking. Which action should the nurse take FIRST?
option_1: Stop the feed, check the tube position and inform the doctor
option_2: Give the feed faster to clear the tube
option_3: Pull the tube out and insert a fresh one at once
option_4: Give some water through the tube and watch
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Stop the feed, check the tube position and inform the doctor

Clinical Rationale: A distended abdomen with no aspirate means the feed is NOT moving on, so the feed is stopped, the tube position is checked and the doctor is told.

Key Clue: a distended abdomen with no aspirate from a nasogastric tube

Priority Principle: Nasogastric feed problem

Why Not Others: (b) A faster feed makes the distension worse; (c) The tube is not pulled out before the position is checked; (d) More water into a full stomach increases the distension.

PGI Exam Trap: The feed is given faster to clear the block.

5-Second Recall: Stop the feed and check the tube.

PNC Exam Pearl: A silent, full abdomen stops the feed.

question: A nurse caring for a family on the ward is asked for the correct definition of a nosocomial infection. Which statement is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: An infection that a patient brings with him into the hospital
option_2: An infection that a patient gets while in hospital for another illness
option_3: An infection that spreads in the village during a season
option_4: An infection that the nurse gets at home from the family
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) An infection that a patient gets while in hospital for another illness

Clinical Rationale: A nosocomial infection is one that the patient picks up during the stay in hospital for some other illness.

Key Clue: the definition of a nosocomial infection

Priority Principle: Nosocomial infection

Why Not Others: (a) An infection brought into the hospital is not a nosocomial one; (c) An infection in the village is a community infection; (d) An infection caught at home is not a hospital infection.

PGI Exam Trap: An infection brought into the hospital is called nosocomial.

5-Second Recall: It is caught during the stay in hospital.

PNC Exam Pearl: Hospital picks up the germ, not the patient.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is to give 500 ml of fluid over 8 hours with a giving set of 20 drops per ml. Which is the MOST appropriate drip rate each minute?
option_1: About 30 drops each minute
option_2: About 15 drops each minute
option_3: About 21 drops each minute
option_4: About 10 drops each minute
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) About 21 drops each minute

Clinical Rationale: The drip rate is the volume in drops divided by the time in minutes, so 10000 drops over 480 minutes is about 21 drops in a minute.

Key Clue: 500 ml over 8 hours with a set of 20 drops per ml

Priority Principle: Drip rate

Why Not Others: (a) Thirty drops in a minute delivers the fluid too quickly; (b) Fifteen drops in a minute delivers the fluid too slowly; (d) Ten drops in a minute is far too slow for this order.

PGI Exam Trap: The drops are divided by the hours to get the rate.

5-Second Recall: Drops in total divided by minutes.

PNC Exam Pearl: Multiply by the drop factor, then divide by the minutes.

question: A nurse caring for a child on the ward explains why play therapy is important for a child in hospital. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It stops the child from crying during the procedures
option_2: It keeps the child busy so that the staff can work
option_3: It teaches the child the lessons of the school
option_4: It helps the child to express fears and to cope with hospital care
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) It helps the child to express fears and to cope with hospital care

Clinical Rationale: Play is the language of the child, so play therapy lets the child show fears and cope better with the hospital and its care.

Key Clue: play therapy for a child in hospital

Priority Principle: Play therapy

Why Not Others: (a) The child may still cry, and play does not prevent that; (b) Keeping the child busy for the staff is not the aim of play therapy; (c) Play therapy is not a school lesson.

PGI Exam Trap: Play therapy is given mainly to keep the child busy.

5-Second Recall: Play lets the child show fears and cope.

PNC Exam Pearl: Play is how a child speaks.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is to give him an intramuscular injection. Which is the BEST order of the steps that the nurse should follow?
option_1: Position the man and then check the order of the drug
option_2: Give the injection FIRST and then explain it to the man
option_3: Prepare the drug and give it without checking the order
option_4: Check the order, explain it to the man, position him, then give it
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Check the order, explain it to the man, position him, then give it

Clinical Rationale: The order is checked FIRST, the man is told about the injection, he is positioned properly, and the injection is then given.

Key Clue: giving an intramuscular injection to a man

Priority Principle: Intramuscular injection

Why Not Others: (a) The check of the order comes before the positioning; (b) The man is told about the injection before it is given; (c) The order is always checked before the drug is prepared.

PGI Exam Trap: The injection is given before the man is told about it.

5-Second Recall: Check the order, explain, position, then give.

PNC Exam Pearl: Check first, always.

question: A nurse caring for an infant whose mother has brought him to the clinic is asked which is the BEST method to assess dehydration. Which method is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Look at the eyes, the skin pinch and the inside of the mouth
option_2: Weigh the infant and compare with the birth weight
option_3: Count the pulse and the breathing of the infant
option_4: Ask the mother how many times he passed urine
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Look at the eyes, the skin pinch and the inside of the mouth

Clinical Rationale: The quickest way to judge dehydration in an infant is to look at the sunken eyes, the slow skin pinch and the dry inside of the mouth.

Key Clue: assessing the dehydration of an infant at the clinic

Priority Principle: Dehydration in the infant

Why Not Others: (b) The weight is useful but needs the earlier weight for a comparison; (c) The pulse and breathing show distress and not the degree of dehydration; (d) The mother's report helps but does not replace the look at the signs.

PGI Exam Trap: The urine count of the mother is the BEST method.

5-Second Recall: Look at the eyes, skin pinch and mouth.

PNC Exam Pearl: Three signs tell the story in an infant.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A man on the ward who takes a potassium supplement now complains of heaviness in the limbs with tingling. Which action is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Give the next dose of the supplement on time
option_2: Stop the supplement and inform the doctor at once
option_3: Massage the limbs well to relieve the heaviness
option_4: Ask him to walk about to improve the circulation
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Stop the supplement and inform the doctor at once

Clinical Rationale: Heaviness and tingling while taking potassium point to too much potassium, so the supplement is stopped and the doctor is told at once.

Key Clue: heaviness in the limbs with tingling in a man on potassium

Priority Principle: Potassium excess

Why Not Others: (a) Another dose raises the potassium further and is dangerous; (c) Massage does not treat the high potassium level; (d) Walking about does not change the potassium level.

PGI Exam Trap: The next dose of potassium is given on time.

5-Second Recall: Stop the drug and inform the doctor.

PNC Exam Pearl: Tingling on potassium means stop it.

Reference Table: Normal serum electrolyte ranges - Sodium (Na+): 135-145 mEq/L; Potassium (K+): 3.5-5.0 mEq/L; Chloride (Cl-): 98-106 mEq/L; Calcium (total): 8.5-10.5 mg/dL; Magnesium (Mg2+): 1.5-2.5 mEq/L; Phosphate: 3.0-4.5 mg/dL.

question: A nurse caring for an incontinent man on the ward explains why the skin is washed and dried gently at every episode. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It makes the ward smell fresh for the visitors
option_2: It keeps the bed linen of the man clean and dry
option_3: Damp skin breaks down quickly and gentle care prevents sores
option_4: It saves the nurse the work of changing the bed
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Damp skin breaks down quickly and gentle care prevents sores

Clinical Rationale: Urine and stools left on the skin break it down quickly, so gentle washing and drying at every episode prevents pressure sores and rashes.

Key Clue: washing and drying the skin of an incontinent man

Priority Principle: Skin care

Why Not Others: (a) The comfort of the man and not the visitors is the aim; (b) Clean linen is a benefit and not the reason for the skin care; (d) The care is given for the skin and not to save the nurse work.

PGI Exam Trap: The gentle washing is done mainly to keep the linen clean.

5-Second Recall: Damp skin breaks down; keep it dry.

PNC Exam Pearl: Dry skin resists the sore.

question: A nurse caring for an unconscious man on the ward gives his dental care with him lying on the side. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It keeps the man warm during the care
option_2: It is easier for the nurse to reach the back teeth
option_3: The fluid can run out of the mouth and will NOT be breathed in
option_4: It stops the man from waking up during the care
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) The fluid can run out of the mouth and will NOT be breathed in

Clinical Rationale: An unconscious patient cannot cough or swallow, so the side position lets the fluid run out of the mouth instead of into the airway.

Key Clue: dental care for an unconscious man in the side position

Priority Principle: Oral care for the unconscious

Why Not Others: (a) Warmth has nothing to do with the position; (b) Reaching the back teeth is not the reason for the position; (d) The position is chosen to protect the airway and not to keep him asleep.

PGI Exam Trap: The side position is used to keep the man warm.

5-Second Recall: Side lying lets the fluid drain out.

PNC Exam Pearl: Side down lets the water out, not in.

question: A man on the ward who takes a monoamine oxidase inhibitor is advised about his diet. Which food should the nurse tell him to avoid?
option_1: Fresh milk and plain curd
option_2: Ripe cheese and other aged foods
option_3: Boiled rice and cooked vegetables
option_4: Fresh fruit and fruit juice
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Ripe cheese and other aged foods

Clinical Rationale: Aged foods such as ripe cheese contain tyramine, which with a monoamine oxidase inhibitor can raise the blood pressure dangerously.

Key Clue: the diet of a man on a monoamine oxidase inhibitor

Priority Principle: Monoamine oxidase inhibitors

Why Not Others: (a) Fresh milk and curd are not high in tyramine; (c) Rice and cooked vegetables are safe with these drugs; (d) Fresh fruit and juice are allowed with these drugs.

PGI Exam Trap: Fresh milk and curd must be avoided with these drugs.

5-Second Recall: Aged cheese carries tyramine and is avoided.

PNC Exam Pearl: Old food and old drug raise the pressure.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a confused man on the ward keeps his bed in the lowest position with the brakes on. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It lowers the chance of a fall and keeps the bed from moving
option_2: It makes the bed easier for the nurse to make
option_3: It keeps the man from getting out of the bed at all
option_4: It saves the space in the ward near the bed
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) It lowers the chance of a fall and keeps the bed from moving

Clinical Rationale: A bed in the lowest position with the brakes on is less likely to be climbed out of and cannot roll away, so the chance of a fall is lowered.

Key Clue: the bed of a confused man kept low with brakes on

Priority Principle: Fall prevention

Why Not Others: (b) Ease of making the bed is not the reason for the low position; (c) The man may still try to get out of the bed; (d) The space in the ward is not the reason.

PGI Exam Trap: The low bed is kept to save space in the ward.

5-Second Recall: A low, locked bed lowers the chance of a fall.

PNC Exam Pearl: Low and locked prevents the fall.

question: A man on the ward is prescribed a tablet to be taken sublingually. Which instruction is the MOST appropriate for the nurse to give him?
option_1: Chew the tablet well and then swallow it
option_2: Swallow the tablet whole with a glass of water
option_3: Crush the tablet and mix it with a little water
option_4: Place the tablet under the tongue and let it dissolve there
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Place the tablet under the tongue and let it dissolve there

Clinical Rationale: A tablet given sublingually is placed under the tongue, where it dissolves and is taken in through the lining of the mouth.

Key Clue: a tablet prescribed to be taken sublingually

Priority Principle: Sublingual administration

Why Not Others: (a) Chewing the tablet is not the sublingual method; (b) Swallowing the tablet loses the benefit of this route; (c) Crushing the tablet is not the sublingual method.

PGI Exam Trap: The tablet is swallowed whole with water.

5-Second Recall: Under the tongue until it dissolves.

PNC Exam Pearl: Sublingual means under the tongue.

question: A nurse caring for a mother on the ward who is breastfeeding is asked which hormone causes the let down of milk. Which hormone is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Oestrogen
option_2: Prolactin
option_3: Oxytocin
option_4: Progesterone
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Oxytocin

Clinical Rationale: Oxytocin causes the muscle of the breast to contract, which pushes the milk out in the let down reflex.

Key Clue: the hormone that causes the let down of milk

Priority Principle: Let down reflex

Why Not Others: (a) Oestrogen is not the hormone of the let down reflex; (b) Prolactin makes the milk and does not let it down; (d) Progesterone is not the hormone of the let down reflex.

PGI Exam Trap: Prolactin causes the let down of the milk.

5-Second Recall: Oxytocin lets the milk down.

PNC Exam Pearl: Prolactin makes milk; oxytocin lets it out.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward with a burn of the leg explains why a bed cradle is used. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It keeps the burnt leg warm through the night
option_2: It keeps the weight of the bed clothes off the burnt leg
option_3: It stops the man from moving the leg in the bed
option_4: It lifts the leg up above the level of the bed
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) It keeps the weight of the bed clothes off the burnt leg

Clinical Rationale: A bed cradle holds the bed clothes above the leg, so nothing presses on the burn and the skin is NOT rubbed or hurt.

Key Clue: a bed cradle for a man with a burn of the leg

Priority Principle: Bed cradle

Why Not Others: (a) Warmth is not the purpose of the cradle; (c) The cradle does not stop the leg from moving; (d) The cradle does not lift the leg itself.

PGI Exam Trap: The cradle is used to keep the burnt leg warm.

5-Second Recall: It holds the bed clothes off the burn.

PNC Exam Pearl: Nothing touches the burn.

question: A nurse caring for a man after surgery explains why he is asked to breathe deeply and cough at regular intervals. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It opens the lungs and clears the mucus that collects after surgery
option_2: It helps the man to sleep better during the night
option_3: It makes the stitches of the wound heal faster
option_4: It keeps the man from feeling sick after the operation
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) It opens the lungs and clears the mucus that collects after surgery

Clinical Rationale: After surgery the lungs do NOT expand fully and mucus collects, so deep breathing and coughing open the lungs and clear the mucus.

Key Clue: deep breathing and coughing after surgery

Priority Principle: Postoperative chest care

Why Not Others: (b) Better sleep is not the reason for the breathing exercises; (c) The wound heals at its own rate and not faster with this; (d) Feeling sick is not prevented by deep breathing.

PGI Exam Trap: Deep breathing is done to make the wound heal faster.

5-Second Recall: It opens the lungs and clears the mucus.

PNC Exam Pearl: Deep breaths keep the chest clear.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked which statement about orthopnoea in a cardiac patient is the MOST appropriate.
option_1: The patient feels giddy when he stands up quickly
option_2: The patient breathes fast only after exercise
option_3: The patient has a cough only in the morning
option_4: The patient cannot lie flat and must sit up to breathe easily
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) The patient cannot lie flat and must sit up to breathe easily

Clinical Rationale: Orthopnoea means that the patient cannot breathe when lying flat and has to sit up to breathe easily.

Key Clue: the meaning of orthopnoea in a cardiac patient

Priority Principle: Orthopnoea

Why Not Others: (a) Giddiness on standing is postural drop and not orthopnoea; (b) Breathlessness after exercise is not what orthopnoea means; (c) A morning cough is a different symptom.

PGI Exam Trap: Orthopnoea means breathlessness only after exercise.

5-Second Recall: The patient must sit up to breathe.

PNC Exam Pearl: Flat means no breath; sitting helps.

question: An elderly confused man on the ward tries to pull out his intravenous cannula at night. Which action is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Tie both his hands to the sides of the bed
option_2: Stay with him, explain gently and cover the cannula site
option_3: Remove the cannula and stop the treatment
option_4: Leave a light on and shut the door of the room
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Stay with him, explain gently and cover the cannula site

Clinical Rationale: A confused man who pulls at the cannula is safest when someone stays with him, explains gently and covers the site so that he cannot reach it.

Key Clue: an elderly confused man pulling at an intravenous cannula

Priority Principle: Cannula safety

Why Not Others: (a) Tying the hands is a restraint and is not the first choice; (c) Removing the cannula stops needed treatment; (d) Shutting the door hides him from the nurses.

PGI Exam Trap: Both his hands are tied to the sides of the bed.

5-Second Recall: Stay with him and cover the site.

PNC Exam Pearl: Watch him and cover, do not restrain.

question: A nurse caring for a man with a urinary catheter on the ward explains why the bag is kept below the level of the bladder. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Urine cannot flow back into the bladder and cause an infection
option_2: The bag is easier for the nurse to empty each shift
option_3: Urine flows out faster when the bag is kept low
option_4: The bag stays hidden from the visitors of the man
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Urine cannot flow back into the bladder and cause an infection

Clinical Rationale: A bag kept below the bladder stops the urine from running back into the bladder, which would carry germs up and cause an infection.

Key Clue: the catheter bag kept below the level of the bladder

Priority Principle: Urinary catheter care

Why Not Others: (b) Ease of emptying is not the reason for the position; (c) The rate of flow does not decide this position; (d) Hiding the bag from visitors is not the reason.

PGI Exam Trap: The bag is kept low to help the urine flow faster.

5-Second Recall: Low bag stops the urine from flowing back.

PNC Exam Pearl: Below the bladder means no back flow.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is to shift him from the bed to a stretcher. Which is the BEST order of the steps that the nurse should follow?
option_1: Ask the man to climb onto the stretcher by himself
option_2: Lift the man up by the arms and carry him across
option_3: Slide the man across while the bed is at its lowest
option_4: Explain, raise the bed to the stretcher level, lock it, then slide him over
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Explain, raise the bed to the stretcher level, lock it, then slide him over

Clinical Rationale: To shift a man safely, the nurse explains the move, raises the bed to the level of the stretcher, locks it and slides him across.

Key Clue: shifting a man from the bed to a stretcher

Priority Principle: Moving the patient

Why Not Others: (a) The man may not be able to climb across by himself; (b) Lifting by the arms is unsafe for the man and for the nurse; (c) Sliding across from a low bed strains the back.

PGI Exam Trap: The man is lifted by the arms to the stretcher.

5-Second Recall: Level the bed, lock it, then slide.

PNC Exam Pearl: Equal heights save the back.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward counts his respirations without telling him. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Counting quietly is the rule of the nursing procedure
option_2: It saves the time taken to explain it to the man
option_3: The rate changes when the man knows that it is being counted
option_4: It keeps the man from asking about his breathing
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) The rate changes when the man knows that it is being counted

Clinical Rationale: A person who knows that the breathing is being counted may change the rate, so the count is taken quietly for a true reading.

Key Clue: counting the respirations without telling the man

Priority Principle: Counting respirations

Why Not Others: (a) The practice is based on accuracy and not on a rule; (b) The time taken is not the reason for the quiet count; (d) Questions from the man are not the reason.

PGI Exam Trap: The respirations are counted quietly to save time.

5-Second Recall: Knowing that it is counted changes the rate.

PNC Exam Pearl: A watched breath is not a true breath.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a man with heart failure explains why his ankles swell more by the evening. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The heart beats faster in the evening than in the morning
option_2: The man drinks more water in the later part of the day
option_3: Gravity pulls the fluid down to the ankles when he is up and about
option_4: The kidneys stop working during the daytime hours
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Gravity pulls the fluid down to the ankles when he is up and about

Clinical Rationale: In heart failure the body holds extra fluid, and standing or sitting through the day lets gravity pull that fluid down to the ankles.

Key Clue: swelling of the ankles in the evening in heart failure

Priority Principle: Oedema in heart failure

Why Not Others: (a) The heart rate does not decide the evening swelling; (b) The amount of water drunk does not explain the evening swelling; (d) The kidneys do not stop working in the daytime.

PGI Exam Trap: The swelling comes from drinking more water in the evening.

5-Second Recall: Gravity pulls the fluid to the ankles.

PNC Exam Pearl: Standing all day sends fluid downwards.

question: A nurse caring for a man with asthma on the ward teaches him to use a peak flow meter. Which is the BEST order of the steps that the nurse should follow?
option_1: Let him blow into the meter while he is lying down
option_2: Ask him to blow out gently into the meter
option_3: Ask him to breathe in and out slowly through the meter
option_4: Stand him up, set the pointer to zero, take a deep breath, then blow hard
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Stand him up, set the pointer to zero, take a deep breath, then blow hard

Clinical Rationale: A peak flow reading is taken standing up, with the pointer at zero, after a deep breath and a hard, short blow into the meter.

Key Clue: teaching a man to use a peak flow meter

Priority Principle: Peak flow meter

Why Not Others: (a) The reading is taken standing and not lying down; (b) A gentle blow gives a false low reading; (c) Slow breathing through the meter is not the test.

PGI Exam Trap: The man blows gently into the meter for the reading.

5-Second Recall: Stand, zero the pointer, deep breath, blow hard.

PNC Exam Pearl: Hard and short gives the true peak.

question: A nurse caring for a man in shock on the ward raises the foot of the bed. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It helps the blood to flow back to the heart and the brain
option_2: It helps the man to breathe more easily in the bed
option_3: It keeps the man warm during the shock
option_4: It stops the man from slipping down the bed
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) It helps the blood to flow back to the heart and the brain

Clinical Rationale: In shock the blood pressure falls, so raising the foot of the bed helps the blood from the legs to flow back to the heart and the brain.

Key Clue: raising the foot of the bed for a man in shock

Priority Principle: Shock

Why Not Others: (b) Breathing is helped by raising the head and not the foot; (c) Warmth comes from covers and not from the position; (d) Slipping down the bed is not the reason for the position.

PGI Exam Trap: The foot of the bed is raised to help the man to breathe.

5-Second Recall: It returns blood to the heart and brain.

PNC Exam Pearl: Feet up sends blood back to the centre.

question: A nurse caring for a man with a convulsive disorder on the ward explains why the side rails are padded. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It keeps him from falling out of the bed at night
option_2: It protects him from injury if he hits the rails during a fit
option_3: It stops him from making a noise during the fit
option_4: It keeps the visitors away from the bed of the man
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) It protects him from injury if he hits the rails during a fit

Clinical Rationale: During a fit the limbs move without control, so padding the rails protects the man from injury when he strikes them.

Key Clue: padding the side rails for a man with a convulsive disorder

Priority Principle: Care during a fit

Why Not Others: (a) The rails themselves prevent the fall; the padding is for injury; (c) The padding does not stop any noise during the fit; (d) Keeping visitors away is not the reason for the padding.

PGI Exam Trap: The padding is put on the rails to keep him from falling out.

5-Second Recall: Padding protects him when he hits the rails.

PNC Exam Pearl: Soft rails mean fewer bruises.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward reads his diet chart, which shows only tea and toast for the last three days with a poor intake. Which interpretation is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The intake is poor and puts the man at risk of weakness and poor healing
option_2: The diet is light and is right for a man who is unwell
option_3: The chart shows that the man needs less food than usual
option_4: The light diet will help the man to recover more quickly
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) The intake is poor and puts the man at risk of weakness and poor healing

Clinical Rationale: Tea and toast for three days give far too little energy and protein, so the man is at risk of weakness and slow healing.

Key Clue: a diet of tea and toast for three days with a poor intake

Priority Principle: Poor dietary intake

Why Not Others: (b) Such a poor intake is not a suitable diet for a sick man; (c) A sick man needs more food for healing and not less; (d) A poor intake delays recovery instead of hastening it.

PGI Exam Trap: The poor intake is taken as suitable for an unwell man.

5-Second Recall: Too little food means weakness and slow healing.

PNC Exam Pearl: Poor food builds a poor recovery.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward after delivery finds that her uterus is NOT contracting, and oxytocin has failed. Which drug is the MOST appropriate to give next?
option_1: Folic acid given by mouth
option_2: Ritodrine given into a vein
option_3: Ethamsylate given by mouth
option_4: Carboprost given into the muscle
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Carboprost given into the muscle

Clinical Rationale: When oxytocin fails to contract the uterus after delivery, a drug such as carboprost is given into the muscle to stop the bleeding.

Key Clue: a uterus that is NOT contracting after oxytocin has failed

Priority Principle: Postpartum haemorrhage

Why Not Others: (a) Folic acid has no action on the uterus after delivery; (b) Ritodrine relaxes the uterus and is the opposite of what is needed; (c) Ethamsylate is not the drug for an atonic uterus.

PGI Exam Trap: Ritodrine is given to contract the uterus.

5-Second Recall: Give carboprost when oxytocin fails.

PNC Exam Pearl: A relaxed uterus needs a contracting drug.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked for the correct angle for inserting a needle for an intradermal injection. Which angle is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: About 90 degrees to the skin
option_2: About 45 degrees to the skin
option_3: About 10 to 15 degrees to the skin
option_4: About 30 degrees to the skin
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) About 10 to 15 degrees to the skin

Clinical Rationale: An intradermal injection is given with the needle almost flat on the skin, at about 10 to 15 degrees, so that it enters the top layer only.

Key Clue: the angle for an intradermal injection

Priority Principle: Intradermal injection

Why Not Others: (a) An angle of 90 degrees is used for an intramuscular injection; (b) An angle of 45 degrees is used for a subcutaneous injection; (d) An angle of 30 degrees is too steep for the skin layers.

PGI Exam Trap: Ninety degrees is used for an intradermal injection.

5-Second Recall: Almost flat, at 10 to 15 degrees.

PNC Exam Pearl: Skin top means a flat needle.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward explains which sample is collected to diagnose pulmonary tuberculosis bacteriologically. Which sample is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The saliva from the mouth
option_2: The sputum coughed out from deep in the chest
option_3: The blood taken into a plain bottle
option_4: The urine passed in the morning
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) The sputum coughed out from deep in the chest

Clinical Rationale: Pulmonary tuberculosis is diagnosed from the sputum coughed out from deep in the chest, because the germ lives in the lungs.

Key Clue: the sample for the diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis

Priority Principle: Sputum for tuberculosis

Why Not Others: (a) Saliva from the mouth is not sputum and gives a wrong report; (c) Blood is not the sample used for this diagnosis; (d) Urine is not the sample for pulmonary tuberculosis.

PGI Exam Trap: Saliva from the mouth is sent for the diagnosis.

5-Second Recall: Sputum from deep in the chest is sent.

PNC Exam Pearl: The germ is in the lung, so send the sputum.

question: A nurse caring for a woman on the ward explains why she is asked to pass urine before an abdominal examination. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: A full bladder is uncomfortable and hides the organs being felt
option_2: It helps the woman to feel less anxious about the test
option_3: It is needed to send a sample to the laboratory
option_4: It prevents the woman from passing urine on the couch
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) A full bladder is uncomfortable and hides the organs being felt

Clinical Rationale: An empty bladder makes the examination comfortable and lets the doctor feel the organs of the abdomen without a full bladder in the way.

Key Clue: passing urine before an abdominal examination

Priority Principle: Abdominal examination

Why Not Others: (b) Anxiety is not the reason for emptying the bladder; (c) A sample is not needed for every abdominal examination; (d) The examination is not done on a couch in this way.

PGI Exam Trap: The bladder is emptied so that a sample can be sent.

5-Second Recall: An empty bladder is comfortable and hides nothing.

PNC Exam Pearl: An empty bladder lets the organs be felt.

question: A nurse caring for a man with chronic kidney disease explains why his skin itches so much. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The man is allergic to the medicines that he takes
option_2: The skin of the man has become very dry from the drugs
option_3: The kidneys are no longer able to keep the skin clean
option_4: Waste products collect in the blood and settle in the skin
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Waste products collect in the blood and settle in the skin

Clinical Rationale: In chronic kidney disease the waste products are NOT cleared, so they collect in the blood and settle in the skin, which causes itching.

Key Clue: itching of the skin in chronic kidney disease

Priority Principle: Itching in renal failure

Why Not Others: (a) An allergy to the medicines is not the usual reason; (b) Dry skin makes it worse but is not the main reason; (c) The kidneys do not keep the skin clean.

PGI Exam Trap: The itching is caused by allergy to the medicines.

5-Second Recall: Waste products settle in the skin and itch.

PNC Exam Pearl: Retained waste irritates the skin.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward who receives oxygen by a mask examines his mouth every day. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The mouth must be clean before the next meal
option_2: The mask may hide a wound on the face of the man
option_3: The oxygen dries the mouth and can cause sores and infection
option_4: The doctor has asked for a daily report on the mouth
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) The oxygen dries the mouth and can cause sores and infection

Clinical Rationale: Oxygen dries the lining of the mouth, so the mouth is examined daily and kept clean to prevent sores and infection.

Key Clue: daily mouth examination for a man on oxygen by mask

Priority Principle: Oral care with oxygen

Why Not Others: (a) Cleaning before a meal is not the reason for the daily check; (b) A wound on the face would be seen when the mask is changed; (d) The daily check is for the safety of the man and not for a report.

PGI Exam Trap: The mouth is checked each day to look for a wound on the face.

5-Second Recall: Oxygen dries the mouth and leads to sores.

PNC Exam Pearl: Dry oxygen, dry mouth, then sores.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the unit explains why eye contact is kept while talking with him. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It keeps the man from looking away during the talk
option_2: It shows interest and helps the man to feel heard and respected
option_3: It helps the nurse to watch for any change in the pupils
option_4: It shortens the time needed for the talk with the man
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) It shows interest and helps the man to feel heard and respected

Clinical Rationale: Kind and steady eye contact shows that the nurse is listening, which helps the man to feel heard and respected.

Key Clue: eye contact while talking with a man

Priority Principle: Therapeutic communication

Why Not Others: (a) The aim is not to stop him from looking away; (c) Watching the pupils is a clinical check and not the reason for eye contact; (d) Eye contact does not shorten the talk.

PGI Exam Trap: Eye contact is kept to watch the pupils of the man.

5-Second Recall: It shows interest and makes him feel heard.

PNC Exam Pearl: Looking at him says that you listen.

question: A nurse caring for a man with asthma on the ward explains why he is asked to hold his breath for a few seconds after using an inhaler. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It helps the man to take in more of the propellant gas
option_2: It prevents the man from coughing after the dose
option_3: It lets the medicine settle in the airways instead of coming out
option_4: It keeps the mouth moist after the medicine is inhaled
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) It lets the medicine settle in the airways instead of coming out

Clinical Rationale: Holding the breath for a few seconds after the dose lets the fine spray settle in the airways instead of being breathed straight out.

Key Clue: holding the breath after using an inhaler

Priority Principle: Inhaler technique

Why Not Others: (a) The propellant gas is not the point of the pause; (b) Preventing a cough is not the reason for holding the breath; (d) Moistening the mouth is not the purpose of the pause.

PGI Exam Trap: The breath is held to prevent a cough after the dose.

5-Second Recall: The pause lets the medicine settle in.

PNC Exam Pearl: Hold, then the spray stays in.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked for the correct definition of dysphagia. Which statement is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Vomiting after every meal
option_2: Pain in the abdomen after eating
option_3: Loss of appetite for all food
option_4: Difficulty in swallowing food or fluid
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Difficulty in swallowing food or fluid

Clinical Rationale: Dysphagia means difficulty in swallowing, in which the food or the fluid does NOT pass easily from the mouth to the stomach.

Key Clue: the definition of dysphagia

Priority Principle: Dysphagia

Why Not Others: (a) Vomiting after a meal is not dysphagia; (b) Pain after eating is not what dysphagia means; (c) Loss of appetite has a different name.

PGI Exam Trap: Loss of appetite is called dysphagia.

5-Second Recall: Dysphagia means difficulty in swallowing.

PNC Exam Pearl: Dys means bad; phagia means swallow.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked about the FIRST step in the assessment of a patient who has fallen in the ward. Which step is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Check whether he is conscious and breathing before moving him
option_2: Lift him back into the bed with the help of others
option_3: Ask him how the fall happened in the ward
option_4: Write the details of the fall in the register
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) Check whether he is conscious and breathing before moving him

Clinical Rationale: After a fall the FIRST step is to check whether the patient is conscious and breathing, and only then to move him.

Key Clue: the assessment of a patient who has fallen in the ward

Priority Principle: Care after a fall

Why Not Others: (b) He is not moved before his condition is checked; (c) The history comes after the safety check; (d) The record is written after the patient is safe.

PGI Exam Trap: The patient is lifted back into the bed at once.

5-Second Recall: Check consciousness and breathing first.

PNC Exam Pearl: Check the patient before you move him.

question: A nurse caring for a child with fever on the ward explains why a tepid sponge is used instead of cold water sponging. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Cold water is harder to find in the ward at night
option_2: Cold water makes the blood vessels shrink and can raise the fever
option_3: Tepid water is quicker to prepare than cold water
option_4: Cold water is too costly for the family of the child
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) Cold water makes the blood vessels shrink and can raise the fever

Clinical Rationale: Cold water makes the blood vessels of the skin shrink, which holds the heat in and may raise the fever, so tepid water is used.

Key Clue: a tepid sponge for a child with fever

Priority Principle: Sponging in fever

Why Not Others: (a) The availability of cold water is not the reason; (c) The time taken to prepare the water is not the reason; (d) The cost to the family is not the reason.

PGI Exam Trap: Cold water is avoided because it is hard to find at night.

5-Second Recall: Cold shrinks the vessels and traps the heat.

PNC Exam Pearl: Cold skin keeps the fever in.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward reads his wound chart, which shows that the wound size has reduced and the tissue is pink and grainy. Which interpretation is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: The wound is healing well with healthy new tissue
option_2: The wound is infected and needs an antibiotic
option_3: The wound has stopped healing and needs a review
option_4: The wound needs to be cleaned more often than now
solution:
Correct Answer: (a) The wound is healing well with healthy new tissue

Clinical Rationale: A wound that is getting smaller with pink, grainy tissue is filling with healthy new tissue and is healing well.

Key Clue: a wound that is smaller with pink grainy tissue

Priority Principle: Wound healing

Why Not Others: (b) An infected wound is red, hot, painful and has discharge; (c) A smaller wound means it is healing and not that it has stopped; (d) More cleaning is not needed for a healthy healing wound.

PGI Exam Trap: A smaller wound with pink tissue is taken as infected.

5-Second Recall: The wound is healing with healthy new tissue.

PNC Exam Pearl: Pink and grainy means the wound is filling.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward is asked for the correct definition of tachycardia in an adult. Which statement is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: A heart rate below 60 beats in a minute
option_2: A heart rate above 100 beats in a minute
option_3: A heart rate between 60 and 100 beats
option_4: A weak and irregular feel of the pulse
solution:
Correct Answer: (b) A heart rate above 100 beats in a minute

Clinical Rationale: Tachycardia in an adult means a heart rate faster than 100 beats in a minute.

Key Clue: the definition of tachycardia in an adult

Priority Principle: Tachycardia

Why Not Others: (a) A rate below 60 is bradycardia; (c) A rate between 60 and 100 is the normal range; (d) A weak irregular pulse describes its quality and not the rate.

PGI Exam Trap: A rate below 60 is called tachycardia.

5-Second Recall: Above 100 beats in a minute is tachycardia.

PNC Exam Pearl: Tachy means fast.

Reference Table: Normal adult vital signs - Temperature: 36.1-37.2 C (97-99 F); Pulse: 60-100 /min; Respiration: 12-20 /min; Blood pressure: < 120/80 mmHg; SpO2: 95-100% (COPD target 88-92%).

question: A nurse caring for a man with a chest tube on the ward explains why the water seal chamber is watched for continuous bubbling. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: Bubbling means that the drainage tube is blocked
option_2: Bubbling shows that the lung has expanded fully
option_3: Continuous bubbling means that air is leaking into the system
option_4: Bubbling shows that the chest tube can be removed
solution:
Correct Answer: (c) Continuous bubbling means that air is leaking into the system

Clinical Rationale: Bubbling on gentle coughing is expected, but continuous bubbling in the water seal means that air is leaking into the system and must be checked.

Key Clue: continuous bubbling in the water seal chamber

Priority Principle: Chest tube care

Why Not Others: (a) A blocked tube stops the bubbling and the drainage; (b) Full expansion is seen on the x ray and not from the bubbling; (d) The tube is not removed because of the bubbling.

PGI Exam Trap: Continuous bubbling is the sign of a blocked tube.

5-Second Recall: Continuous bubbling means an air leak.

PNC Exam Pearl: Bubbles that never stop mean a leak.

question: A nurse caring for a man on the ward after a long bed rest explains why he is taught to rise from the bed in stages. Which reason is the MOST appropriate?
option_1: It helps the man to stretch his muscles before he walks
option_2: Rising slowly keeps the man from falling back on the bed
option_3: It gives the nurse time to reach the side of the bed
option_4: Rising slowly prevents the blood pressure from falling and giddiness
solution:
Correct Answer: (d) Rising slowly prevents the blood pressure from falling and giddiness

Clinical Rationale: After a long bed rest the blood pressure falls on standing, so rising in stages lets the body adjust and prevents giddiness and a fall.

Key Clue: rising from the bed in stages after a long bed rest

Priority Principle: Postural hypotension

Why Not Others: (a) Stretching is useful but not the main reason; (b) Falling back is a result and not the reason for the slow rise; (c) The reason is the safety of the man and not the time for the nurse.

PGI Exam Trap: He rises in stages so that the nurse has time to reach him.

5-Second Recall: Stages prevent the pressure from falling.

PNC Exam Pearl: Rise slowly, or the head will swim.
